utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I just moved to Nashville and look who came to visit me. She said that I'm going to starve to death down here if I don't learn how to cook. So today we're going to learn how to fix cornbread. What's the most important step?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah, you can read, can't you?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Well yeah, I can read, man. Got our egg and our milk. Let's take a big old sip of that egg, girl.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: When you break an egg, if it's a farm fresh egg, you always want to break it in a cup because if you don't, it could be bad because hens don't know to get off of them. They think they're their babies. I got some. There's your pro chicken tip there, young man Roberts.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Now, wait a second. I saw this chef online say that the secret to the best Nashville cornbread is a big spoonful of white sugar in the batter. Let's get that in there.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Put that spoon down. We are not making cake, we are making cornbread. If you put sugar in that bowl, I am walking out of this kitchen right now and you can starve in peace.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: But Grandma, it balances the salt! It's the new way of doing it for the vlog.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I don't care about a 'vlog.' I care about your soul. We are going to sit here and stare at this batter until you realize that sugar has no business in a skillet. I'm waiting. You want to cook, or you want to play?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: All right, I got my batter in here. Now I'm going to put some pepper in here. What do you think? How do you think it's going to taste, man?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Mm, good. Okay. Mm, here, try that.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Oh, oh, that's good. I don't think I'm going to be starving now.
